purpose: Continuation of the country x subject occupation-salary research matrix. Same integrity rule: only occupation-level sources may populate a subject figure; a country or sector figure is NEVER shown as a subject figure. Findings that cannot be sourced at occupation level are recorded as gaps with the reason, never estimated.
basis_convention: GROSS medians, whole occupation, all experience levels. Not entry-level, not degree-specific, not take-home.

us-bls-oews-2025-05.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics - Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) / Occupational Outlook Handbook

uk-ons-ashe-2025-provisional.publisher: Office for National Statistics - Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) 2025 provisional
uk-ons-ashe-2025-provisional.extraction_note: The occupation-level medians were located through independent re-publishers of the ONS ASHE 2025 provisional table (values cross-checked and identical across at least three). Promotion to the validated corpus requires confirmation directly against the primary ONS ASHE Table 14 xlsx; the figure is recorded here as OFFICIAL_STATISTICS but flagged for primary confirmation. ONS suppresses small cells rather than estimating them.

ie-cso-earnings-2025.publisher: Central Statistics Office (Ireland) - Earnings and Labour Costs
ie-cso-earnings-2025.granularity_note: CSO publishes earnings by economic SECTOR and by BROAD occupational category (e.g. 'Managers, professionals and associated professionals'), NOT by detailed occupation. No occupation-specific pay source exists for the launch subjects, so Ireland subject-level pay is a GAP. Sector/broad figures (e.g. Information & Communication hourly labour cost) are NOT subject-level and must never be displayed as such.

au-jsa-osca-2026-04.publisher: Jobs and Skills Australia - Occupation and Industry Profiles (OSCA/ANZSCO), based on ABS data
au-jsa-osca-2026-04.granularity_note: Employment counts are published by occupation, but median weekly earnings are explicitly NOT produced for many detailed occupations (out-of-scope list). Occupation-specific medians are published for only some ANZSCO unit groups.

claims.statement: In the United States, software developers (SOC 15-1252) had a median annual wage of USD 135,980 (mean USD 148,100; 10th pct USD 82,460; 90th pct USD 214,670) in May 2025, across 1,687,890 jobs.
claims.demand: Projected employment growth 10% (2025-2035), much faster than average; about 106,100 openings per year.
